title: Motion of a hopping body in the background of a recording medium

key_results.statement: For a start with all $\phi_h\neq0$: $d_0(h,h')=\lim_{\lambda\to0^+}\alpha(h,h';\lambda)/\lambda=\lVert u_h-u_{h'}\rVert$ with $u_h=(K_h-\langle K_h\rangle)\chi$, independent of the hopping amplitudes $t_{hh'}$.

For every place $k$: $\lVert\bar x(\lambda)-u_k\rVert^2=\sum_hp_h(\lambda)\,d_0(h,k)^2-s(\lambda)^2$, and $s(\lambda)^2=\tfrac12\sum_{h,h'}p_h(\lambda)\,p_{h'}(\lambda)\,d_0(h,h')^2$. The spread $s$ is well defined; $\bar x$ and $v$ are well defined up to the common isometry $e^{i\varphi}$ of the background embedding, so all their $g$-invariants are.

$\frac{\mathrm dp_h}{\mathrm d\lambda}=\sum_{h'}J_{h'\to h}$ exactly, with the antisymmetric current $J_{h'\to h}(\lambda)=2\operatorname{Im}[t_{hh'}(V_b(\lambda))_{h'h}]=-J_{h\to h'}$, which vanishes off the edges of the hopping graph.

$\lvert J_{h'\to h}(\lambda)\rvert\le2\lvert t_{hh'}\rvert\sqrt{W(h,h';\lambda)\,p_h(\lambda)\,p_{h'}(\lambda)}\le2\lvert t_{hh'}\rvert\sqrt{p_hp_{h'}}$; no current flows across a completely witnessed edge ($W=0$).

$v(\lambda)=\sum_{\{h,h'\}\in E}2\operatorname{Im}[t_{hh'}(V_b(\lambda))_{h'h}]\,(u_h-u_{h'})$, a sum over the edges of the hopping graph in which each term is independent of the orientation of its edge.

For every start and every $\lambda$: $\lVert v(\lambda)\rVert\le v_{\max}:=\varrho(a)\le\max_h\sum_{h'}\lvert t_{hh'}\rvert\,d_0(h,h')$, where $a_{hh'}=\lvert t_{hh'}\rvert\,d_0(h,h')$ and $\varrho(a)$ is the largest eigenvalue of $a$; hence $\lVert\bar x(\lambda_2)-\bar x(\lambda_1)\rVert\le v_{\max}\lvert\lambda_2-\lambda_1\rvert$.

For the start $\phi=\lvert\beta\rangle$ and $h\neq\beta$: $p_h(\lambda)=\lambda^2\lvert t_{h\beta}\rvert^2+\lambda^3\operatorname{Im}[t_{h\beta}^*(t^2)_{h\beta}]+\lambda^4p_h^{(4)}+O(\lambda^5)$, and $p_\beta=1-\sum_{h\neq\beta}p_h$, where the $\lambda^3$ terms cancel in $p_\beta$.

The records $K_h$ enter $p_h$ first at $\lambda^4$, in $p_\beta$ and in the neighbours of $\beta$; for $h\neq\beta$, $p_h^{(4)}=\tfrac14\lvert(t^2)_{h\beta}\rvert^2-\tfrac13\operatorname{Re}[t_{h\beta}^*(t^3)_{h\beta}]-\tfrac1{12}\lvert t_{h\beta}\rvert^2d_0(h,\beta)^2-\tfrac1{12}\lvert t_{h\beta}\rvert^2(\epsilon_h-\epsilon_\beta)^2+\tfrac16\sum_{h'}\operatorname{Re}(t_{h\beta}^*t_{hh'}t_{h'\beta})(\epsilon_h+\epsilon_\beta-2\epsilon_{h'})$ with $\epsilon_h=\langle K_h\rangle$, where the first two terms do not depend on the records and the genuine record part is $-\tfrac1{12}\lvert t_{h\beta}\rvert^2d_0(h,\beta)^2\le0$.

For the start $\phi=\lvert\beta\rangle$: $\bar x(\lambda)-u_\beta=\lambda^2w_2+\lambda^3w_3+O(\lambda^4)$ with $w_2=\sum_h\lvert t_{h\beta}\rvert^2(u_h-u_\beta)$ and $w_3=\sum_h\operatorname{Im}[t_{h\beta}^*(t^2)_{h\beta}](u_h-u_\beta)$.

For pairwise commuting $K_h=\sum_j\kappa_h(j)P_j$: $V_b(\lambda)=\sum_jw_j\,U_j(\lambda)\lvert\phi\rangle\langle\phi\rvert U_j(\lambda)^\dagger$ with $U_j(\lambda)=e^{-i(C_b+D_j)\lambda}$, $D_j=\sum_h\kappa_h(j)\lvert h\rangle\langle h\rvert$ and $w_j=\langle\chi\vert P_j\vert\chi\rangle$: the view is a $w_j$-weighted mixture of record-free hopping evolutions.

On the infinite chain $h_m$, $m\in\mathbb Z$ (the limit of long finite chains), with hopping amplitude $t>0$ between neighbouring places, $K_{h_m}=mX$ with $X=\sum_\xi\xi\,\Pi_\xi$, $w_\xi=\langle\chi\vert\Pi_\xi\vert\chi\rangle$, $\sigma_X^2=\langle X^2\rangle-\langle X\rangle^2>0$ and the start $\lvert h_0\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$: $p_{h_m}(\lambda)=\sum_\xi w_\xi\,J_m\bigl(z_\xi(\lambda)\bigr)^2$ with Bessel functions $J_m$ and $z_\xi(\lambda)=\frac{4t}{\xi}\sin\frac{\xi\lambda}{2}$ ($z_0=2t\lambda$).

On the chain of (17.18) with the start $\lvert h_0\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$: $\bar x(\lambda)=u_{h_0}=0$ (so $v\equiv0$) and $s(\lambda)^2=4t^2\sigma_X^2\sum_\xi w_\xi\,\frac{1-\cos\xi\lambda}{\xi^2}$, where the $\xi=0$ term of the fraction is read as $\lambda^2/2$.
On the chain of (17.18), $d_0(h_m,h_n)=\lvert m-n\rvert\,\sigma_X$, and the bound of (17.7) is $v_{\max}=2t\sigma_X$.

On the chain of (17.18) with the start $2^{-1/2}(\lvert h_0\rangle+e^{i\theta}\lvert h_1\rangle)\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$, real $\theta$ and $e=(X-\langle X\rangle)\chi$: $\bar x(\lambda)=\Bigl[\tfrac12+t\sum_\xi w_\xi\,\frac{\cos\theta-\cos(\theta-\xi\lambda)}{\xi}\Bigr]e$, where the $\xi=0$ term of the fraction is read as $-\lambda\sin\theta$.

For the start of (17.21): $v(\lambda)=t\sum_\xi w_\xi\sin(\xi\lambda-\theta)\,e=t\operatorname{Im}[e^{-i\theta}\langle\chi\vert e^{iX\lambda}\vert\chi\rangle]\,(X-\langle X\rangle)\lvert\chi\rangle$, hence $\lVert v\rVert\le t\sigma_X=v_{\max}/2$.

On the chain of (17.18) with the start $\lvert h_0\rangle\otimes\lvert\chi\rangle$: $\sup_\lambda s(\lambda)<\infty$ iff $\Pi_0\lvert\chi\rangle=0$ (that is, $\chi\perp\ker X$), and then $s^2\le8t^2\sigma_X^2\sum_{\xi\neq0}w_\xi/\xi^2$. Under the same condition the position $\bar x_{(b)}$ for the start of (17.21) stays bounded, $\lVert\bar x_{(b)}-\tfrac12e\rVert\le2t\sigma_X\sum_{\xi\neq0}w_\xi/\lvert\xi\rvert$.

definitions.name: Position of the body in the background
Spread of the body in the background
Velocity (rate of change of the position with respect to λ)

open_issues: Item 3: for places at graph distance n ≥ 2 only the leading term and the bound that the records enter not before λ^(2n+1) are given; the leading order of x̄ − u_β when w₂ = w₃ = 0 is not determined in general (in example 5(a) it vanishes identically).
The speed bound (17.7) is not shown to be attained; in example 5(b), ‖v‖ ≤ v_max/2.
Position and velocity are measured in the fixed background built from the start χ (definition in the question); how the witness geometry at finite λ deviates from λ d₀ is not addressed.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions and conservation: [t] = [K] = 1/[λ] gives [u_h] = [d₀] = 1/[λ] and [v] = 1/[λ]² = [t d₀] in (17.7); λ⁴|t|²d₀² in (17.10) and z_ξ are dimensionless; ∑_h dp_h/dλ = 0 by antisymmetry of the current; the λ³ terms of (17.9) cancel in p_β.

Trivial limits: without hopping J = 0, v = 0, v_max = 0 and all coefficients in (17.9)–(17.13) vanish, consistent with p_h = δ_{hβ}; with all K_h equal the state stays a product and the view is record-free, so d₀ = 0, v_max = 0, x̄ is constant and the K-dependent part of (17.10) vanishes.

Item 3 against item 5: expanding (17.18) for m = 1 gives p_{h₁} = t²λ² − (t⁴ + t²⟨X²⟩/12)λ⁴ + O(λ⁶), which agrees with (17.10) for (t²)_{h₁h₀} = 0, (t³)_{h₁h₀} = 3t³, no common neighbour and d₀² + (ε₁ − ε₀)² = ⟨X²⟩.
